chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: Dispute with her managers Gladys and Claude
summary: Gladys initiated legal proceedings and Maxine's pay was held in escrow after she signed with Columbia's management bureau.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Excuse me. Did you have a three-way contract when you came to New York? Is that what happened?
No, I had no contract. I signed with Gladys and Claude --
Yes, that's what I mean. The three of you were partners of some sort.
Right. Well Gladys and Claude were my managers. But Gladys sort of stayed on the sidelines. She had very little, if any, input into the early efforts. Claude did all the work.
But when I went out to Hollywood to do the picture and also to open the club -- when I got there, there was a wire there saying to hold my salary up in lieu of settlement.
She initiated legal proceedings?
That's right. And, of course, by that time I was already signed with Columbia, because actually Claude -- neither Claude nor Gladys were in a position to handle

me on a larger scale. By this time, Claude had seen that I'd signed up with Columbia. So I was under Columbia management, and they had their percentage -- what they were supposed to get. They were paid out of whatever my salary was.
Now, this is not connected with the record company.
Yeah. Columbia had the records and --

At that time, Columbia had its management bureau, it had the records. Columbia -- later on, Columbia had to give up their management bureau because of so-called monopolistic tendencies. But anyway, there was a possibility that I was going to begin to make some money. So therefore, Gladys sort of stepped in and I -- Claude was strictly a musician. He was not concerned about these things. But Gladys probably felt that, you know, this is time and sort of make some ripples. So when I got out there, my salary was
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
held in escrow, and I was paid a certain amount a week. My money was in escrow for about three more years because I had a five-year contract with them.

And -- so the money was being held in escrow in lieu of a settlement. It was kind of sticky there for awhile, because Claude had not been interested, you know. They were going to get their money anyway.
But there might've been some -- I don't know -- maybe they didn't think that Columbia knew that they had a piece of me, so to speak.
Yeah.
So they wanted to let them know. So my money was held in escrow.
Can you recollect how big the piece was?
Yes, twenty-five percent. That was what I had signed with them, see.
Divided equally between them?
Well, I don't know how they did it. That was their problem. I don't know whether they had a little spat or what.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yeah.

I would think that probably Gladys began to needle Claude and it all came to a head. But it -- as I said, my salary was held in escrow and I was receiving a certain amount a week to manage on. I don't know why it had to -- I guess it was settled out of court, or something. But they got their money. We had to wait until the time was up. But anyway, this caused a little -- put a little wedge in our relationship -- the relationship with Claude, because we were pretty tight. Claude was very sincere. He did everything, you know, to further my career. But I imagined he became aware that maybe there was more to it than appeared on the surface. And so we sort of fell out. I don't know. I really don't know. It was sad for me. I hated to lose Claude. But I imagined in order for them to pursue the case, we couldn't be on subtly terms. We had

to be friendly enemies, or something like that.

But anyway, that was the end of our relationship. He didn't make any more arrangements for me. These last selections -- "I Dream of Jeannie" -- "I'm Happy About the Whole thing." "Drink To Me Only With Thine Eyes" and "Corn Pickin' was the last session we made together.
